correctness.rationale: In the orthonormal basis trap a, antipode b, and uniform shell s of the m remaining vertices, the hopping matrix has couplings g=J√m from s to each of a,b, zero a–b coupling, and shell diagonal h=J(m−2). The orthogonal complement is invariant and has no trap component. On the three-dimensional space an undamped eigenvector of the loss generator would have zero trap component by 2 Re(λ)||v||²=−κ|v_a|². Its trap row then forces its shell component to vanish, and its shell row forces its b component to vanish. Thus the restricted generator is Hurwitz and capture is certain from b. An adjacent vertex has bright squared norm 1/m. Independently I solved B†Y+YB=−I for the integrated-survival operator and found Y_bb=3/κ+κ(2+h²/g²)/(4g²). Substituting g,h gives the displayed rational expression, whose strictly positive coefficient of κ gives the unique optimum and whose size limit follows at fixed J,κ. The nearby complete-bipartite catalogue entry does not falsify n=2: an independent four-site integrated-density solve confirmed exactly coherent E[T]=3/κ+κ/(4J²) and, for positive off-diagonal dephasing γ, E[T]=4/κ+3κ/(8J²)+γ/J². The right-hand limit is larger by 1/κ+κ/(8J²); the exact-zero and limiting regimes are not interchangeable. The issue in the other entry is its identification of those regimes, not this frozen formula.

value.rationale: Capture of a nonadjacent source is known, but that alone gives no bound on the duration. This exact first moment establishes bounded time with fixed per-edge hopping as the dense graph grows and exhibits the tradeoff between weak loss and slow capture at very strong loss, with an explicit optimal strength for every size. It is a useful solvable benchmark for the coherent trap, not a re-evaluation of known capture efficiencies or evidence for a general bounded-time theorem.
residual_risks: The hopping scale is held fixed per edge; normalization by the degree or adding dephasing can change the time behavior. The coherent value is not justified by extrapolation from dephasing.
